title: Muuyawkatsina - Moon Spirit
description: Illustration of Muuyawu, a Kachina moon spirit of the Hopi People of Southern Arizona - widely considered one of the oldest living cultures in the world. Originally by Gerald Dawavendewa (Hopi & Cherokee).
process: Started with a pencil sketch of the figure and traced over that with fine liners of different weights. Red circle made with acrylic, painted flat and left to dry. It was a joy to try and find the perfect shade by mixing and experimenting.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. I just loved the expression of the figure, reminiscent of a traveller of the nights.
meaning: Something about being watched over at night by an entity that slightly unsettles you. The figure isn't doing anything — just being present, looking into you.

title: Taawakatsina - Sun Spirit
description: My reimagination of Taawa, the sun spirit of the Hopi People regarded as the creator of the First World and a guide through existence. Often associated with fertility, life and growth.
process: Rough pencil sketch traced on with fine liners. Used different hatching techniques to create visual complexity and depth. I chose a lush deep green to represent the sun.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. They usually have feline features and the sun spirit looked particularly playful just floating around.
meaning: To me, they represent the will of life, radiating out.

title: Tree of Life
description: My highly simplified take on the classic Tree of Life motif seen in various artforms across the country. Representing the interconnectedness of all life. This was a gift to my fiance's grandmother so it needed extra care and patience. I tried to incorporate elements that dont usually go into this sort of imagery, like the sky or the arches.
process: Rough pencil sketch of half of the tree made on tracing paper and mirrored on the other side to create symmetry then traced on with fine liners. Used the finest point liner to hatch and dot, something I greatly enjoy doing.
inspiration: Tree of life motif in Pattachitra style of Odisha. Border is a common pattern in Madhubani. The gold represents the fruits of life.
meaning: It means family and beauty. Projecting our hopes into the future.

title: Taawaventiwa
description: A precession of planets, with Taawa - the sun spirit in the center. Tuuwaqatsi (Earth, the Fourth World) travels with Muuyaw - the Moon spirit below. The Hopi people call the 22 Degree Halo sometimes seen circling the sun Taawaventiwa, believing to bring light and fertility.
process: Sketched out with pencil and traced with fine liner. Used acrylic pens and paints. I took some creative liberties with the colouring illustrating day on the left with dragonflies and night on the right with stars.
inspiration: Heavily inspired by Gerald Dawavendewa's series on the Kachina.
meaning: I think it was a fitting 3rd illustration representing the Sun and Moon spirit together.

title: Cellular
description: This is a cell that has captured various types of bacteria and has formed an obligate relationship with them. The neucleus is a writhing cloud of radioactive matter that powers the cell while the catured bacteria and cytoplasm act as control structures, absorbing excess neutrons to moderate the energy generated by the core. The external membraine of the cell is covered with tiny stalks that each contain a packet of energy, which can be used by other cells in exchange for resources like sugars, fats and protiens.
process: Saw this on Pintrest and in Making this, I wanted to test my patience. The goal was to put as much detail in as I could while still retainig the organic feel of the cell. Took me around 10 hours.
inspiration: I think in a way I was inspired by my anxiety. This was a way for me to get lost in the details and forget about the world for a few hours. I obsessed over every dot, line and colour.
meaning: I think it was a fitting 3rd illustration representing the Sun and Moon spirit together.
